hook.text: The central United States sees more tornadoes than anywhere else on Earth—a region nicknamed Tornado Alley.

buildup.text: Warm, moist air from the Gulf of Mexico clashes with cold, dry air from Canada across the Great Plains.

discovery.text: The Rocky Mountains add dry air aloft, creating a 'cap' that builds instability until explosive storms erupt.

twist.text: Tornado Alley is shifting—recent research shows the highest activity is moving eastward into the Southeast.

climax.text: Dixie Alley, from Mississippi to Tennessee, now rivals the Plains for tornado frequency—and has higher fatality rates.

punchline.text: Tornado Alley isn't fixed—it's slowly moving east.

quiz.question: Why does Tornado Alley have so many tornadoes?
options: Collision of Gulf moisture with cold Canadian air and Rocky Mountain effects
